Subject: Optimizing unit economics — phased rollout + credits proposal for ZenithAI

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I sketched two pragmatic paths to reduce per-token spend during your initial model rollout while keeping latency under 150ms P50 for inference on customer queries:

Option A — Operational credits + conservative quantization
- 20% one-time credit applied to first 6 months of billed inference usage
- Run standard 8-bit post-training quantization (INT8) on our verified Llama-2-variant; minimal accuracy delta on your chat prompts (we ran your sample corpus)
- Default batching at 16 reqs with prefix caching tuned for short conversation tails

Option B — Commit + aggressive batching and mixed precision
- 12-month reserved commit (discount stepped by utilization) + 10% onboarding credit
- Mixed quantization profile: 4-bit where we preserve key layers in 8-bit; likely ~1.6x token cost reduction but requires MR test on your eval sets
- Enable longer batching windows for asynchronous flows (up to 120ms extra latency budget)

Attachments: zenithai-credits-vs-discount-matrix.xlsx (matrix), redwood-optimize-playbook-v1.pdf (technical appendix).

Questions for you:
1) Is the latency SLO above firm for all traffic or only for high-priority routes?
2) Would you prefer a stop-gap credits-first approach while we run the MR evals, or do you want the commit-based route locked in before launch?

Proposed next step: 30-minute walkthrough of the matrix + a quick demo of quantization A/B results (Karthik can join to walk the kernel-level tradeoffs).

Best,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Mina —

Appreciate the clear options and the spreadsheet. Quick clarifications from my side before we book the walkthrough:

- Latency SLO: for our real-time support routing, 150ms P50 is firm; for analytics/batch summarization we can accept higher P95 in the 400-600ms band. We likely want two routing classes.
- Traffic mix: ~65% low-context messages (short history), ~35% long multi-turn (>=512 tokens).
- Procurement: we prefer starting with a 6-mo pilot and then expand; credits-first sounds attractive — procurement will need a defined scope & MPO/PO line item.

Two technical Qs for Karthik:
1) For the mixed quantization you mention, what's the risk window for hallucination/regression on Q/A? We have a 5% accuracy regression guardrail.
2) If we adopt prefix/KV caching, how does that interact with privacy needs? We cannot persist customer-provided PII outside our VPC — will caching be fully in our control on Redwood Private?

If you can answer these, I'll align procurement and we can set the walkthrough.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Platform Partnerships — ZenithAI

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Optimizing unit economics — phased rollout + credits proposal for ZenithAI

Alex —

Short answers to your technical questions, plus a recommendation.

1) Mixed quantization accuracy risk:
- We run a layer-wise sensitivity scan during quantization. For the L2-like models we onboarded, keeping attention and first/last feedforward layers at 8-bit while quantizing the majority to 4-bit kept accuracy loss < 2% on intent-classification and retrievalQA suites; for open-ended generation the variance is higher.
- To meet your 5% guardrail we recommend: A/B the mixed profile on your representative eval set (we do the runs) and hold back any profile that exceeds 3% measured degradation.

2) KV/prefix caching & privacy:
- On Redwood Private, caching is tenant-local and honors your KMS/HSM keys — nothing leaves your VPC unless you opt into hosted features. We provide config knobs: ephemeral-only caching (in-memory; TTL < 2 min) vs. durable caching (encrypted at rest).
- For PII, we recommend ephemeral caching + request-side redaction pipelines during the pilot. We can instrument a mode where the cache stores only hashed prefixes for routing efficiency while full context is sent to the model.

Recommendation: start with Option A (credits + INT8) for the pilot to preserve baseline accuracy; in parallel run the mixed-quant MR suite on a sample of long-turn traffic. If MR passes your 3% internal threshold, switch traffic routing for non-real-time routes to the mixed profile and convert credits into a partial commit credit.

I'll prepare short sample runs (5k tokens) and share result screenshots prior to the walkthrough.

— Karthik
Senior Applied ML, Redwood Inference
